reason: The text explicitly demonstrates the Hebrew people expressing their views and having those views honored. Specifically, Pharaoh tells Moses and Aaron 'Take your journey, and serve the LORD as you have said' (כְּדַבְּרְכֶם - 'as you have spoken'), indicating that their request to depart and serve God had been expressed and was being granted. The passage describes the systematic enactment of the people's expressed desires regarding the Exodus. This directly contradicts the claim that the Hebrew people are discouraged from expressing their views; rather, it shows their expressed views being heard and acted upon.
